26V621000:
Chrysler (FCA US, LLC) is recalling 265,512 vehicles because water may enter the electric power steering wiring harness, which can disable power steering assist, according to a filing NHTSA received on Sept. 29, 2026. The recall, campaign number 26V621000, covers certain Ram ProMaster and ProMaster BEV vehicles from model years 2022 through 2026.

The filing lists the affected vehicles as 2022-2026 Ram 1500 ProMaster, Ram 2500 ProMaster and Ram 3500 ProMaster models, and 2024-2026 Ram 3500 Electric vehicles. The component involved is the electric power assist steering system. NHTSA's filing states that a loss of power steering assist can increase the risk of a crash. The filing does not specify whether any crashes or injuries have been reported.

According to the filing, dealers will inspect the vehicles and replace the wiring harness and the electronic power steering gear as necessary, free of charge. The filing does not specify how long the repair will take or when the final remedy will be available. The record lists "Do not drive" and "Park outside" as "No," meaning no such instruction was issued with the recall.

Chrysler's interim notification letters to owners are expected to be mailed Nov. 17, 2026, and additional letters will be sent once the final remedy is available. Vehicle identification numbers for the recall became searchable on NHTSA.gov on Oct. 6, 2026. Owners may contact Chrysler customer service at 800-853-1403 and refer to Chrysler's recall number, 92D.
26V630000:
Volkswagen Group of America, Inc. is recalling 22,524 model year 2023 through 2026 ID.4 vehicles because the high voltage battery may fail and lead to a vehicle fire, according to a filing the company submitted to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. NHTSA received the report on Sept. 30, 2026, and lists the campaign number as 26V630000. Volkswagen's number for the recall is 93EX.

The recall covers the traction battery, part of the vehicles' electrical and propulsion systems. NHTSA's filing states that a vehicle fire increases the risk of injury. The filing does not specify whether any fires, crashes or injuries have occurred, or what causes the battery failure. The record lists the recall as neither a "do not drive" nor a "park outside" notice.

Until a repair is completed, owners are advised to charge their vehicles to a maximum of 80% battery capacity, according to the corrective action described in the filing. The remedy is currently under development, and the filing does not specify when it will be available or what it will involve.

Volkswagen expects to mail interim letters notifying owners of the safety risk on Nov. 27, 2026, with additional letters to follow once the remedy is available. Owners may contact Volkswagen customer service at 1-800-893-5298. Vehicle Identification Numbers involved in the recall became searchable on NHTSA.gov on Oct. 6, 2026.
26V633000:
Honda is recalling 4,206 motorcycles because the fuel pump may malfunction due to a manufacturing defect, according to a filing the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received on Oct. 1, 2026. The recall covers certain 2023-2025 VT1300CX and 2024-2025 VT750 models, and is listed under NHTSA campaign number 26V633000.

The affected component is the gasoline fuel delivery system's fuel pump. NHTSA's filing says fuel pump failure can cause an engine stall, increasing the risk of a crash. The filing does not specify whether any crashes or injuries have been reported, or how many pumps have failed.

The filing lists neither a do-not-drive instruction nor a park-outside instruction for owners. As the remedy, dealers will replace the fuel pump free of charge. The filing does not say how long the repair will take or when replacement parts will be available.

Honda, filing as American Honda Motor Co., will mail owner notification letters beginning Nov. 27, 2026. Vehicle Identification Numbers involved in the recall will be searchable on NHTSA.gov beginning Oct. 8, 2026. Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-866-784-1870 and refer to Honda's recall number, KU9.
26V636000:
Mercedes-Benz USA is recalling four 2027 Mercedes-Benz CLA 220 vehicles because a component of the left front seat belt may have been installed incorrectly, according to a filing the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received on Oct. 2, 2026. The recall is identified by NHTSA campaign number 26V636000, and the affected component is listed as front seat belts.

NHTSA's record states that a seat belt with an incorrectly installed component may fail to properly restrain occupants, increasing the risk of injury during a crash. The record does not specify whether any crashes or injuries have been reported, and it does not state how the incorrect installation occurred.

The filing lists 4 potentially affected vehicles. It indicates that owners are not advised to stop driving the vehicles or to park them outside. As the remedy, the manufacturer says dealers will inspect the seat belt and replace it as necessary, free of charge.

Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed Nov. 27, 2026. Owners may contact Mercedes-Benz USA customer service at 1-800-367-6372. The filing does not specify how long the inspection or replacement will take.
26V638000:
Mercedes-Benz USA, LLC is recalling 30,064 vehicles in the U.S. because the front brake hoses may rupture and leak brake fluid, according to a recall report NHTSA received on Oct. 2, 2026. The recall, campaign number 26V638000, covers certain 2022 through 2025 model-year S-Class vehicles. Mercedes-Benz USA says the company is recalling the vehicles.

The filing lists the S 500 4MATIC, Maybach S 580 4MATIC, Maybach S 680 4MATIC and S 580 4MATIC for model years 2022 to 2025. It also lists the S 580 E 4MATIC for 2023 to 2025 and the AMG S 63 E Performance for 2024 and 2025. NHTSA classifies the affected component as service brakes, hydraulic: foundation components. The manufacturer's filing says a brake fluid leak can extend the distance needed to stop the vehicle, increasing the risk of a crash. The filing does not say whether any crashes or injuries have been reported, and it does not state what causes the hoses to rupture.

The record states that the vehicles are not under a do-not-drive or park-outside advisory. Dealers will replace the front brake hoses free of charge. The filing does not specify how long the repair will take or when replacement parts will be available. The recall expands an earlier NHTSA recall, number 25V116.

Mercedes-Benz USA expects to mail owner notification letters on Nov. 27, 2026. Owners may contact the company's customer service at 1-800-367-6372. According to the filing, the vehicle identification numbers involved in the recall became searchable on NHTSA.gov on Oct. 9, 2026.
AQ26002:
NHTSA opened an audit query on September 3, 2026, into how Tesla certified its Cybercab, a vehicle the agency's record lists as the 2026 Tesla Robotaxi (Cybercab), as compliant with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. The action number is AQ26002, and the subject is "Tesla Cybercab FMVSS Certification." The agency says it is examining the process and technical data Tesla relied on when certifying the vehicles, along with related issues.

According to NHTSA's summary, Tesla began commercial deployment of a small number of Cybercab vehicles in Austin, Texas, on September 3, 2026. Tesla notified the agency that it certified those vehicles as compliant with all applicable FMVSS. Tesla also told NHTSA it plans to gradually expand commercial deployment to include additional vehicles and locations.

The record states that the vehicles lack permanently attached, conventional manual controls, such as a brake pedal, gas pedal, steering wheel and mirrors. NHTSA says it will consider, among other things, the extent to which Tesla's certification depended on determinations that certain FMVSS are inapplicable to the Cybercab.

An audit query is the investigation type listed for this action. NHTSA's filing does not specify how many vehicles are covered, whether any crashes or injuries have occurred, or when the review is expected to conclude. The filing also does not describe any remedy or required action by Tesla.
DP26008:
NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened a defect petition, DP26008, on September 3, 2026, into the 2.0 Liter EcoBoost engine in 2015 through 2018 Ford Edge vehicles. The subject of the investigation is loss of motive power, and the component category is engine and engine cooling. The manufacturer is Ford Motor Company.

According to the filing, ODI received the petition on August 5, 2026. The petition alleges that engine coolant intrusion results in a significant loss of engine power, accompanied by an "Engine Coolant Over Temperature" warning message. The petition further alleges that after the vehicle has sat and cooled down, the engine runs roughly and generates a check engine light for a cylinder misfire.

NHTSA said the petition was opened to evaluate the issue and determine whether to grant or deny it. The filing does not specify how many vehicles are covered, and it does not say whether any crashes, injuries or complaints are linked to the alleged problem. It also does not include a statement from Ford.

The record lists no remedy, and no repair timeline was specified in NHTSA's filing. The next step stated in the record is the agency's decision on whether to grant or deny the petition. The petition can be reviewed at NHTSA.gov under ODI number 11754989.
DP26009:
NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened a defect petition, DP26009, on September 14, 2026, into the driveshaft-to-rear-differential connection on 2022 BMW 540i vehicles. According to the agency's record, the petitioner alleges the vehicles are experiencing a sudden mechanical failure that severs the drive connection between the driveshaft and the rear wheels. The component is listed as power train: driveline: driveshaft, and the manufacturer is BMW of North America, LLC.

ODI received the petition on September 1, 2026. The petition is dated August 5, 2026, and requests an investigation into an alleged defect in BMW rear differential assemblies. NHTSA states it opened the petition to evaluate the issue and determine whether to grant or deny it. The petition can be reviewed at NHTSA.gov under ODI number 11761650.

BMW filed Safety Recall 26V525 on August 12, 2026, according to the record. NHTSA's summary does not say how many vehicles the recall covers or whether it addresses the same condition described in the petition. The filing also does not describe the remedy, a repair timeline, or when owners would be notified.

NHTSA's record does not specify any crashes, injuries or fatalities connected to the alleged failure. It also does not say how many 2022 BMW 540i vehicles are affected or what causes the failure. The next step stated in the record is ODI's decision on whether to grant or deny the petition.
DP26010:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened a defect petition on Oct. 9, 2026, to evaluate a request for an investigation into Tesla's model year 2026 Robotaxis. The petition alleges that the vehicles' Automated Driving System exceeds posted speed limits in active school zones, according to NHTSA's filing. The agency's Office of Defects Investigation is reviewing the allegation under action number DP26010.

The vehicles covered are the Robotaxi versions of the Model Y and the Cybercab, both model year 2026 and built by Tesla, Inc. NHTSA lists the component as the electrical system, specifically the software for the advanced driver assistance, autonomous or self-driving function. The allegation applies to vehicles with the Automated Driving System engaged.

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation received the petition on Sept. 23, 2026. The petitioner provided three links to video footage as supporting evidence. The agency opened the defect petition to evaluate the allegations and determine whether to grant or deny the petition. The petition can be reviewed on NHTSA.gov under ODI Number 11766676.

NHTSA's filing does not specify how many vehicles are affected, whether any crashes or injuries have been reported, or what remedy might be required. It also does not include a statement from Tesla or a timeline for the agency's decision on the petition.
RQ26003:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's Office of Defects Investigation opened a Recall Query on Oct. 9, 2026, into detachment of the upper grille deflector on 2022 through 2024 model year GMC Sierra 1500 trucks. The agency said it has received 118 complaints alleging the part detaches. The investigation is numbered RQ26003, and the manufacturer is General Motors, LLC.

According to NHTSA's summary, the complaints allege the upper grille deflector detaches while the vehicle is being driven. The agency said that in some cases this led to a cracked windshield or to surrounding vehicles needing to make evasive maneuvers. NHTSA's filing lists the affected component as the active shutters and grille, under bumpers and body structure. The record does not specify any crashes or injuries.

Of the 118 complaints, 21 allege the deflector detached after Recall 25V-060 had been performed on the vehicle. GM submitted that recall to NHTSA on Feb. 6, 2025. It addressed upper grille deflector detachment on 2022 model year GMC Sierra vehicles built with a chrome grille deflector. According to NHTSA, 2022 Sierras not built with a chrome grille deflector, and all 2023 and 2024 model year Sierras, were not included in the recall.

NHTSA said it opened the Recall Query to assess the adequacy of the scope and the remedy for Recall 25V-060. The filing does not describe the recall remedy, say how many vehicles are affected, or give a timeline for the review. It also includes no statement from GM. NHTSA's filing says the ODI reports cited in the investigation can be reviewed at NHTSA.gov.
